content.content:
1	# Chat/RAG Requirements Quality Checklist: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
2	
3	**Purpose**: Pre-implementation requirements-quality review covering RF04's four main requirement clusters — streaming/failure/retry state machine, offline & connectivity behavior, side menu sessions (list/pagination/titling), and RAG grounding & persistence semantics — ahead of `/speckit-tasks`.
4	**Created**: 2026-10-19
5	**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)
6	
7	**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
8	**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
9	**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.
10	
11	## Requirement Completeness
12	
13	- [ ] CHK001 Are requirements defined for an SSE connection that fails to establish at all (before `message_created`), as distinct from a mid-stream drop? [Gap, Spec §FR-004/FR-005]
14	- [ ] CHK002 Is the behavior specified for a retry request that itself returns an immediate non-streaming error (e.g., 4xx) before any streaming begins? [Gap, Spec §FR-006]
15	- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements defined for what the composer/UI shows between the user tapping send and the lazily-created session's `POST /chat/sessions` response arriving? [Gap, Spec §FR-010]
16	- [ ] CHK004 Is there a requirement for what the side menu shows while the first page of `GET /chat/sessions` is still loading (empty state vs. loading indicator)? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]
17	- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements defined for the local cache's retention limits (if any) across previously-opened conversations, or is unbounded retention an implicit assumption? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
18	- [ ] CHK006 Is a requirement defined for the case where `POST /chat/sessions` succeeds but the following first-message send fails, leaving a session that exists with no messages? [Gap, Edge Cases]
19	
20	## Requirement Clarity
21	
22	- [ ] CHK007 Is "most recent activity" (`lastUserMessageAt`) ordering unambiguous for two sessions sharing an identical timestamp, so side-menu/pagination order is stable? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
23	- [ ] CHK008 Is the "short, trimmed preview" title-derivation rule (length, truncation boundary, whitespace handling) specified precisely enough for two implementers to produce identical output? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010, Assumptions]
24	- [ ] CHK009 Is "near the backend's maximum length" in the message-length edge case quantified with the actual numeric limit the client must enforce or detect? [Clarity, Edge Cases]
25	- [ ] CHK010 Is the "standard no-connection state" shown for a never-cached conversation (FR-011, Edge Cases) specified with enough detail to distinguish it from the offline banner shown over a cached conversation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]
26	
27	## Requirement Consistency
28	
29	- [ ] CHK011 Do FR-007 (single-flight gating per conversation) and FR-012 (block create/send/retry while offline) combine consistently for the case of being offline while a response is already in flight for that same conversation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007/§FR-012]
30	- [ ] CHK012 Is the terminal-state vocabulary in FR-004 ("complete response" / "Falha ao gerar resposta") consistent with the Key Entities section's "still arriving, complete, or failed" status language? [Consistency, Spec §Key Entities]
31	- [ ] CHK013 Is the offline-cache scope in FR-011 ("every previously-opened conversation") fully reconciled with the Edge Cases statement about a never-opened conversation, leaving no undefined partially-cached state in between? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011]
32	- [ ] CHK014 Is "Novo Chat"'s behavior while offline (FR-009) consistent with FR-010's lazy-creation model and FR-012's block-on-offline rule, or does the spec leave an implicit third case unaddressed? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009/§FR-010/§FR-012]
33	
34	## Acceptance Criteria Quality
35	
36	- [ ] CHK015 Can SC-001's "100% of tested cases" be objectively verified without a documented minimum sample size or seeding procedure? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
37	- [ ] CHK016 Is SC-004's "zero observed duplicates" across "repeated retries" measurable without the spec specifying how many repeated retries constitute a sufficient test? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
38	- [ ] CHK017 Does SC-006's "re-enabling within one interaction of connectivity returning" define what counts as "one interaction" precisely enough to be testable (e.g., does a passive reconnect count, or only a user-initiated retry)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
39	- [ ] CHK018 Does SC-007 define a specific session-count threshold used to verify "remains reachable by scrolling," or is the test condition left to the reviewer's discretion? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]
40	
41	## Scenario Coverage
42	
43	- [ ] CHK019 Are requirements defined for retrying a message that failed mid-stream (partial text present) versus one that failed before any token arrived — is the retry-triggering UI treatment specified as identical in both cases? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006]
44	- [ ] CHK020 Is single-flight gating (FR-007) explicitly scoped to "per conversation," with a requirement covering whether a user can send in a different, idle conversation while another conversation's response is still in flight? [Clarity/Gap, Spec §FR-007]
45	- [ ] CHK021 Are requirements defined for retrying a message that is no longer in the error state by the time the retry call resolves (e.g., state changed via another device or session)? [Gap, Edge Cases]
46	- [ ] CHK022 Are requirements defined for the account's very-first-ever message, where no session yet exists and the RAG-grounding context (User Story 1) has no prior entries at all to draw on? [Coverage, Spec §Assumptions]
47	
48	## Edge Case Coverage
49	
50	- [ ] CHK023 Is there a requirement for connectivity dropping and returning more than once while a single response is still streaming? [Gap, Edge Cases]
51	- [ ] CHK024 Are requirements defined for cache staleness — if a cached session's history could diverge from the backend once connectivity returns, is a refresh required, or is the cache treated as authoritative until the user reopens the session? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
52	- [ ] CHK025 Is the side menu's pagination requirement (FR-008) explicit about behavior when a cursor-paginated fetch fails mid-scroll (retry automatically, inline error, or silent stop)? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]
53	- [ ] CHK026 Is behavior specified for the app being backgrounded mid-stream and resumed — does the requirement rely solely on the existing "reflects whatever the backend ultimately recorded" rule (Edge Cases), or is a distinct resume/reconnect case needed? [Gap, Edge Cases]
54	
55	## Non-Functional Requirements
56	
57	- [ ] CHK027 Are performance expectations defined for the optimistic local message appearing after tap-to-send, distinct from the network-dependent streaming latency that follows it? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions, Plan Performance Goals]
58	- [ ] CHK028 Are accessibility requirements (e.g., assistive-technology announcement of streaming → complete/error transitions) defined for chat message state changes? [Gap, Coverage]
59	- [ ] CHK029 Are requirements defined for how the session-expiration overlay (FR-013) interacts with an in-progress SSE stream specifically, beyond the general "history and scroll position preserved" statement already covering static views? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013]
60	
61	## Dependencies & Assumptions
62	
63	- [ ] CHK030 Is the assumption that "a session always has a `lastUserMessageAt` by the time it is listed" (Clarification 2) validated against the lazy-creation flow's actual ordering of session-creation and first-message-send calls? [Assumption, Spec Clarification 2]

# Chat/RAG Requirements Quality Checklist: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)

**Purpose**: Pre-implementation requirements-quality review covering RF04's four main requirement clusters — streaming/failure/retry state machine, offline & connectivity behavior, side menu sessions (list/pagination/titling), and RAG grounding & persistence semantics — ahead of `/speckit-tasks`.
**Created**: 2026-10-19
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are requirements defined for an SSE connection that fails to establish at all (before `message_created`), as distinct from a mid-stream drop? [Gap, Spec §FR-004/FR-005]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the behavior specified for a retry request that itself returns an immediate non-streaming error (e.g., 4xx) before any streaming begins? [Gap, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements defined for what the composer/UI shows between the user tapping send and the lazily-created session's `POST /chat/sessions` response arriving? [Gap, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK004 Is there a requirement for what the side menu shows while the first page of `GET /chat/sessions` is still loading (empty state vs. loading indicator)? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements defined for the local cache's retention limits (if any) across previously-opened conversations, or is unbounded retention an implicit assumption? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK006 Is a requirement defined for the case where `POST /chat/sessions` succeeds but the following first-message send fails, leaving a session that exists with no messages? [Gap, Edge Cases]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK007 Is "most recent activity" (`lastUserMessageAt`) ordering unambiguous for two sessions sharing an identical timestamp, so side-menu/pagination order is stable? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the "short, trimmed preview" title-derivation rule (length, truncation boundary, whitespace handling) specified precisely enough for two implementers to produce identical output? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK009 Is "near the backend's maximum length" in the message-length edge case quantified with the actual numeric limit the client must enforce or detect? [Clarity, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the "standard no-connection state" shown for a never-cached conversation (FR-011, Edge Cases) specified with enough detail to distinguish it from the offline banner shown over a cached conversation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK011 Do FR-007 (single-flight gating per conversation) and FR-012 (block create/send/retry while offline) combine consistently for the case of being offline while a response is already in flight for that same conversation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007/§FR-012]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the terminal-state vocabulary in FR-004 ("complete response" / "Falha ao gerar resposta") consistent with the Key Entities section's "still arriving, complete, or failed" status language? [Consistency, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the offline-cache scope in FR-011 ("every previously-opened conversation") fully reconciled with the Edge Cases statement about a never-opened conversation, leaving no undefined partially-cached state in between? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK014 Is "Novo Chat"'s behavior while offline (FR-009) consistent with FR-010's lazy-creation model and FR-012's block-on-offline rule, or does the spec leave an implicit third case unaddressed? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009/§FR-010/§FR-012]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK015 Can SC-001's "100% of tested cases" be objectively verified without a documented minimum sample size or seeding procedure? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK016 Is SC-004's "zero observed duplicates" across "repeated retries" measurable without the spec specifying how many repeated retries constitute a sufficient test? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK017 Does SC-006's "re-enabling within one interaction of connectivity returning" define what counts as "one interaction" precisely enough to be testable (e.g., does a passive reconnect count, or only a user-initiated retry)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK018 Does SC-007 define a specific session-count threshold used to verify "remains reachable by scrolling," or is the test condition left to the reviewer's discretion? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK019 Are requirements defined for retrying a message that failed mid-stream (partial text present) versus one that failed before any token arrived — is the retry-triggering UI treatment specified as identical in both cases? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK020 Is single-flight gating (FR-007) explicitly scoped to "per conversation," with a requirement covering whether a user can send in a different, idle conversation while another conversation's response is still in flight? [Clarity/Gap, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK021 Are requirements defined for retrying a message that is no longer in the error state by the time the retry call resolves (e.g., state changed via another device or session)? [Gap, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK022 Are requirements defined for the account's very-first-ever message, where no session yet exists and the RAG-grounding context (User Story 1) has no prior entries at all to draw on? [Coverage, Spec §Assumptions]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK023 Is there a requirement for connectivity dropping and returning more than once while a single response is still streaming? [Gap, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK024 Are requirements defined for cache staleness — if a cached session's history could diverge from the backend once connectivity returns, is a refresh required, or is the cache treated as authoritative until the user reopens the session? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK025 Is the side menu's pagination requirement (FR-008) explicit about behavior when a cursor-paginated fetch fails mid-scroll (retry automatically, inline error, or silent stop)? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK026 Is behavior specified for the app being backgrounded mid-stream and resumed — does the requirement rely solely on the existing "reflects whatever the backend ultimately recorded" rule (Edge Cases), or is a distinct resume/reconnect case needed? [Gap, Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK027 Are performance expectations defined for the optimistic local message appearing after tap-to-send, distinct from the network-dependent streaming latency that follows it? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions, Plan Performance Goals]
- [ ] CHK028 Are accessibility requirements (e.g., assistive-technology announcement of streaming → complete/error transitions) defined for chat message state changes? [Gap, Coverage]
- [ ] CHK029 Are requirements defined for how the session-expiration overlay (FR-013) interacts with an in-progress SSE stream specifically, beyond the general "history and scroll position preserved" statement already covering static views? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK030 Is the assumption that "a session always has a `lastUserMessageAt` by the time it is listed" (Clarification 2) validated against the lazy-creation flow's actual ordering of session-creation and first-message-send calls? [Assumption, Spec Clarification 2]
- [ ] CHK031 Is the dependency on RF03/RF07's existing "Sessão expirada" overlay (FR-013) validated to already cover expiry occurring specifically mid-SSE-stream, not only during static history viewing? [Assumption, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK032 Is the assumption that chat's write-call error presentation "follows the same retryable/non-retryable pattern already established project-wide (RNF09)" validated against SSE-specific failure modes, such as a stream erroring after partial tokens were already delivered? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK033 Does the spec bound how much or which prior content counts as "relevant" for grounding (User Story 1), or is relevance entirely opaque to the client with no observable contract? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK034 Does the spec clarify whether a response that found no relevant prior entries is client-distinguishable from a grounded one, given FR-001's "MUST be able to reflect" language implies grounding is not guaranteed on every response? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK035 Is "chat messages are conversational only" (FR-003) explicit about whether it excludes only entry-creation, or also other automatic side effects (e.g., analytics, proactive-insight triggers) not otherwise named in this unit's scope? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference

625	2. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1 (lazy session creation, send, stream, persist, no entry created).

627	   restart the app and confirm the exchange persists (SC-005).
628	4. Demo/ship if ready — this alone delivers RF04's "entire premise" (spec.md, User Story 1's "Why this
629	   priority").
630

# Tasks: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/007-chat-memory-rag/`
**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md (all present)

**Tests**: Included. `plan.md`'s Constitution Check marks RNF07 (domain coverage ≥80%) and RNF09 (Either +
15/15 error scenarios) both "PASS (gate carried into tasks)", and every file under `contracts/` carries its own
"Test scenarios this contract owns" table plus `quickstart.md`'s "Automated checks" section — this is this
feature's own design material requesting test tasks, not an invented addition.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story (spec.md's five User Stories: P1, P1, P2, P2, P3). This
feature introduces one entirely new feature folder (`lib/features/chat/`, two blocs) plus two `core/network/`
extensions. Loading a conversation (resume-last / switch / new-empty) is needed by every single story — even
US4's "Novo Chat" and US5's offline browsing go through the same `_loadSession` path — so the shared
transport/data/repository layer and `ChatBloc`'s own "load a conversation" machinery are necessarily
Foundational; each User Story phase then adds that story's own handler bodies, widgets, and tests on top.

## Path Conventions

Single Flutter project (plan.md's "Project Type"): `lib/features/chat/{domain,data,presentation}/`, mirrored
under `test/features/chat/...`; two `core/network/` files extended in place; `lib/features/home/` extended in
place. No `backend/`/`frontend/` split, no `.env`/native project file touched, no change to
`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` (Constraints, FR-014).

---

## Phase 1: Setup

No setup tasks. `plan.md`'s "Primary Dependencies" is explicit — "No additions... reuses the full existing
stack" — and the Project Structure's "Structure Decision" already fixes every new file's location. Proceed
directly to Foundational.

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: the shared transport (`SseFrame`/`ApiClient.sseStream`, live connectivity), the domain entities,
the data layer (`ChatRemoteDataSource`/`ChatLocalCache`/`ChatRepositoryImpl`), and `ChatBloc`'s own
"resume/switch/new empty conversation" machinery (`ChatStarted`/`ConversationSelected`/
`NewConversationRequested`/`_loadSession`) that every user story's handlers build on top of.

**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story phase can begin until this phase is complete.

- [ ] T001 [P] Create `lib/core/network/sse_frame.dart`: `class SseFrame extends Equatable` with `final String
  event` and `final String data` (raw JSON text, parsed by the caller — `ApiClient` itself stays generic),
  `props => [event, data]` (data-model.md, contracts/sse-transport-extension.md).

- [ ] T002 Extend `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` with `Stream<Either<Failure, SseFrame>> sseStream(String
  function, {required String method, Map<String, dynamic>? body, List<String>? pathSegments, AuthMode authMode
  = AuthMode.userSession})` per contracts/sse-transport-extension.md: issues the request via
  `_dio.request<ResponseBody>(url, options: Options(method: ..., responseType: ResponseType.stream, headers:
  {'apikey': _anonKey, 'Authorization': 'Bearer $bearer'}))` (same header-building logic `call()` already
  uses); decodes each byte chunk as UTF-8 (`allowMalformed: true`) into a buffer and splits frames on the
  blank-line (`\n\n`) SSE delimiter, parsing `event:`/`data:` lines per frame (multiple consecutive `data:`
  lines joined with `\n`; any other SSE field ignored); yields `Right(SseFrame(...))` per parsed frame in
  arrival order; on `DioException`, yields **exactly one** `Left(_mapException(e))` — reusing the existing
  `_mapException` verbatim, no second failure-mapping implementation — as the stream's **last** item, then the
  stream closes (no further iteration of `response.data!.stream` after the exception). `call()` is unchanged.
  Depends on T001.

- [ ] T003 Create `test/core/network/api_client_sse_test.dart` per contracts/sse-transport-extension.md's "Test
  scenarios this contract owns" table: scenario #1 (3 frames split across 2 byte chunks mid-frame — all 3 parsed
  correctly, no dropped/duplicated bytes across the boundary); #2 (a `DioException` with `type: connectionTimeout`
  thrown after 1 frame already yielded — exactly `Right(frame1)` then `Left(NetworkTimeoutFailure)` as the
  stream's last item); #3 (a `DioException` with no `response` at all — `Left(NetworkOfflineFailure)` as the
  final item); #4 (a frame containing only `event: context\ndata: {}` — yielded as an ordinary
  `Right(SseFrame(event: 'context', data: '{}'))`, since the generic transport never special-cases an event
  name); #5 (a multi-line `data:` field split across two consecutive `data:` lines — both joined with `\n` into
  one `SseFrame.data`). Mock the underlying `dio` stream response the same way `api_client_test.dart`'s existing
  `call()` tests already mock `Dio`. Depends on T002.

- [ ] T004 [P] Add `Stream<bool> get onConnectivityChanged` to `lib/core/network/connectivity_checker.dart`
  (research.md R8): wraps `Connectivity().onConnectivityChanged`'s own broadcast stream, mapping "any result
  `!= ConnectivityResult.none`" → `true` — the exact same predicate `hasConnection()` already uses. The existing
  synchronous `hasConnection()` method is unchanged (R8's own write-path pre-check still calls it directly).

- [ ] T005 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_session.dart`: `enum ChatPersona { analitico,
  empatico, socratico }`; `class ChatSession extends Equatable` with `required` fields `id` (`String`), `title`
  (`String`), `personaSnapshot` (`ChatPersona` — read-only here, FR-014, never written back), `userMessageCount`
  (`int`), `lastUserMessageAt` (`DateTime?` — "nullable per schema; in practice always non-null once listed"),
  `createdAt`/`updatedAt` (`DateTime`); `props` over all seven fields (data-model.md).

- [ ] T006 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_message.dart`: `enum ChatRole { user, assistant
  }`; `enum ChatMessageStatus { streaming, complete, failed }`; `class ChatMessage extends Equatable` with
  `required` fields `id` (`String` — `'local-<timestamp>'`-prefixed until reconciled with the server's real id,
  research.md R5), `sessionId`, `role`, `content` (grows incrementally while `status == streaming`), `seq`
  (`int`), `status`, `retryCount` (`int`), `createdAt`; `bool get isOptimistic => id.startsWith('local-')`;
  `props` over `[id, sessionId, role, content, seq, status, retryCount, createdAt]` (data-model.md).

- [ ] T007 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_sessions_page.dart`: `class ChatSessionsPage
  extends Equatable` with `final List<ChatSession> sessions` and `final String? nextCursor` (`meta.nextCursor`
  verbatim; `null` = last page) — directly mirrors `EntriesPage`'s own shape. Depends on T005.

- [ ] T008 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_stream_event.dart`: `sealed class ChatStreamEvent
  extends Equatable`; `MessageCreated({required String userMessageId, required String assistantMessageId})`;

- [ ] T009 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_title_deriver.dart`: `class ChatTitleDeriver`
  with a private constructor, `static const _maxLength = 48`, and `static String derive(String
  firstMessageText)` — collapses internal whitespace/newlines to single spaces via `replaceAll(RegExp(r'\s+'),
  ' ')`, trims, and when the result's length exceeds 48 returns `'${collapsed.substring(0, 48)}…'`, otherwise
  the collapsed string unchanged. Pure, total; never returns an empty string for non-empty input; no
  `package:flutter` import, no I/O (research.md R6, Principle V).

- [ ] T010 Create `lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart`: abstract `ChatRepository` with
  `Future<Either<Failure, ChatSession>> createSession({required String title})`; `Future<Either<Failure,
  ChatSessionsPage>> listSessions({String? cursor, int? limit})`; `List<ChatSession> get cachedSessions`;
  `Future<Either<Failure, List<ChatMessage>>> listMessages(String sessionId)`; `List<ChatMessage>?
  cachedMessages(String sessionId)` (`null` = this session's history was never fetched while online); `Future<void>
  setLastActiveSessionId(String? sessionId)`; `Future<String?> get lastActiveSessionId`; `Stream<Either<Failure,

  `Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>> retryMessage({required String sessionId, required String

- [ ] T011 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/data/chat_local_cache.dart` (research.md R4): Keychain-backed

- [ ] T012 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/data/chat_remote_data_source.dart` per contracts/chat-repository.md:
  `ChatRemoteDataSource(this._apiClient)`; `createSession({required title})` → `_apiClient.call

  first-ever use) — using a seeded prior entry
  (`docs/input/backend/fixtures/seeded-search-entries.md`) and an account with more sessions than one
  `chat-sessions-list` page. Depends on T053.

---

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: no dependencies — can start immediately. **BLOCKS** every user story phase (every
  story needs `ChatBloc`'s "load a conversation" machinery at minimum).
- **User Story 1 (Phase 3)**: depends on Foundational only. MVP.
- **User Story 2 (Phase 4)**: depends on Foundational **and** US1's `_consumeTurn` (T022) — its failure-handling
  branch is built as part of that same function and cannot be split; this phase is otherwise test-only.
- **User Story 3 (Phase 5)**: depends on Foundational and US1's `_consumeTurn` (T022), which it reuses verbatim
  for the retry's own stream consumption.
- **User Story 4 (Phase 6)**: depends on Foundational only — independent of US1/US2/US3's own tasks (no shared
  code with `ChatBloc`'s turn-consumption machinery).
- **User Story 5 (Phase 7)**: depends on Foundational's `_loadSession`/`ChatSessionsBloc` cache-fallback logic
  (already built there) and on `ChatComposer` (T023, US1) for its own offline-disabling test.
- **Polish (Phase 8)**: depends on all five user stories being complete.

### Within Each Phase

- Tasks touching the *same* file (`chat_bloc.dart`, `home_chat_shell_page.dart`, `app_drawer.dart`,
  `service_locator.dart`, `app_router.dart`) are listed in the sequential order they must be applied.
- Tasks creating a *new* file with no dependency on that phase's other new files are marked `[P]`.
- Test tasks are marked `[P]` relative to each other (distinct test files); each still depends on its
  corresponding implementation task(s) existing to pass.

### Parallel Opportunities

- T001, T004–T009, T014, T015, T017 (Foundational's entities/events/states/widgets/transport) can all run in
  parallel — ten independent files with no cross-dependencies among them.
- T011 and T012 (local cache, remote data source) can run in parallel with each other once T001–T009 land.
- All test tasks within a single user story phase can run in parallel with each other.
- User Story 4 (side menu) can be implemented in parallel with User Stories 1–3 (the live conversation) by a
  second developer, since neither `ChatSessionsBloc` nor `AppDrawer`'s "CONVERSAS" section shares any code path
  with `ChatBloc`'s turn-consumption machinery.

---

## Parallel Example: Foundational Phase

```bash
# Launch the independent entity/transport/widget files together:
Task: "Create SseFrame in lib/core/network/sse_frame.dart"
Task: "Add onConnectivityChanged to lib/core/network/connectivity_checker.dart"
Task: "Create ChatSession/ChatPersona in lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_session.dart"
Task: "Create ChatRole/ChatMessageStatus/ChatMessage in lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_message.dart"
Task: "Create ChatStreamEvent in lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_stream_event.dart"
Task: "Create ChatTitleDeriver in lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_title_deriver.dart"
Task: "Create ChatEvent in lib/features/chat/presentation/bloc/chat_event.dart"
Task: "Create ChatMessageBubble in lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_message_bubble.dart"
```

---

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)

1. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (transport, data layer, entities, `ChatBloc`'s conversation-loading core).
2. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1 (lazy session creation, send, stream, persist, no entry created).
3. **STOP and VALIDATE**: seed a prior entry, send a related message, confirm the grounded response (SC-001);
   restart the app and confirm the exchange persists (SC-005).
4. Demo/ship if ready — this alone delivers RF04's "entire premise" (spec.md, User Story 1's "Why this
   priority").

### Incremental Delivery

1. Foundational → User Story 1 (MVP: grounded, persisted conversation).
2. + User Story 2 (the three-state visual contract — mostly tests over already-built engine behavior).
3. + User Story 3 (tap-to-retry on a failed response).
4. + User Story 4 (side menu: list, paginate, "Novo Chat") — independently buildable in parallel with 2–3.
5. + User Story 5 (offline banner + multi-conversation offline coverage).
6. + Polish (verification gates, manual walkthrough).

Each stage adds value without breaking the previous one, matching spec.md's own stated priority order (P1, P1,
P2, P2, P3).

# Implementation Plan: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)

**Branch**: `007-chat-memory-rag` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; none of this repo's extension
hooks are configured, per spec.md's own header)

**Date**: 2026-10-19 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/007-chat-memory-rag/spec.md`, `docs/input/requirements.md` §1
(RF04), §6.3 (`chat-sessions-create`/`chat-sessions-list`/`chat-messages-list`/`chat-messages-send`/
`chat-messages-retry`), §8 (data model reference), §9 (stack), §10 (no new fixed parameter for this unit),
§13; `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`'s `/chat/sessions*` schemas; `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`;
`docs/input/backend/README.md`'s function-name mapping; `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §§2.2
("Tela 1 — Home/Chat", "Tela 3 — Menu lateral"), 3, 4, 6; and `.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Depends on
F000 (`specs/001-foundation/`) and RF03 (`specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/`), both already implemented — this
is the unit that makes Home/Chat's currently-inert, fully-disabled composer (F000's own scaffold,
`home_chat_shell_page.dart`) and the side menu's currently-static `AppDrawer` actually work.

## Summary

Home/Chat gains a live, persisted conversation with the backend's RAG-grounded agent
(`POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`, SSE: `message_created -> context -> token* -> done|error`), and the side
menu's `AppDrawer` gains a paginated, offline-cached "CONVERSAS" list (`GET /chat/sessions`) plus a working
"Novo Chat" action. A new feature folder, `lib/features/chat/`, is added with its own three-layer structure:
`ChatSession`/`ChatMessage`/`ChatSessionsPage`/`ChatStreamEvent`/`ChatTitleDeriver` (domain), `ChatRemoteDataSource`/
`ChatLocalCache`/`ChatRepositoryImpl` (data), and two blocs — `ChatBloc` (the one live conversation: streaming,
retry, lazy session creation, composer gating) and `ChatSessionsBloc` (the side menu's own paginated list,
mirroring `RecordsBloc`'s RF07-established shape almost exactly, research.md R7). `core/network/ApiClient`
gains one new, chat-agnostic method, `sseStream()`, built on `dio`'s own `ResponseType.stream` with a
hand-rolled SSE frame parser (research.md R1) — no new package. `core/network/ConnectivityChecker` gains a
live `onConnectivityChanged` stream (research.md R8), layered on top of (not replacing) the existing
synchronous `hasConnection()` pre-check every write path in this app already uses. A new, Keychain-backed
`ChatLocalCache` (mirroring `EntriesLocalCache`'s own pattern) persists the session list, each individually-
opened session's message history, and the last-active session id, satisfying spec.md's Clarification 3
(offline browsing covers every previously-opened conversation, not just the one open at disconnect) and its
own Assumptions (resuming the last conversation on app restart). A new chat message or its own session is
never created eagerly — only lazily, at the moment a first message is actually sent (FR-010) — and the title
sent with that creation call is derived client-side from the message's own text by a new, pure
`ChatTitleDeriver` (research.md R6), since the backend has no auto-titling or rename endpoint of its own. No
new `go_router` route is added: Home/Chat stays the one existing, unparameterized `/home` screen, swapping its
displayed conversation in place via the two blocs it's now provided with (research.md R7) — "Novo Chat" and
selecting a past conversation from the drawer are both in-place state transitions, not navigations.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from
F000/RF01/RF02/RF03/RF06/RF07.

**Primary Dependencies**: No additions. Reuses the full existing stack — `flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `get_it`,
`equatable`, `dio` (via `ApiClient`, extended with `sseStream()`), `go_router` (no new route), `flutter_secure_storage`
(for the new `ChatLocalCache`), `connectivity_plus` (its own `onConnectivityChanged` stream, previously
unused — `ConnectivityChecker` only ever called `checkConnectivity()` once per check before this unit); dev-only
`mocktail`, `bloc_test`. SSE is consumed via a ~30-line hand-rolled parser over `dio`'s existing byte-stream
support, explicitly chosen over any third-party SSE package (research.md R1) — the OpenAPI contract's own
schema for both SSE operations is `content: text/event-stream` / `{type: string}`, i.e. genuinely no typed
shape to generate a client from.

**Storage**: One new on-device store, `ChatLocalCache` (research.md R4) — three independent
`flutter_secure_storage` keys (`chatSessionsLocalCache`, `chatMessagesLocalCache`, `chatLastActiveSessionId`),
same Keychain-backed, JSON-encoded mechanism `EntriesLocalCache` (RF01) already established for personal
content. No local database, no new third-party persistence package.

**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` + `mocktail`, unchanged tooling. Coverage via
`fvm flutter test --coverage`, same `lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter (RNF07), now additionally exercising
`chat_title_deriver.dart` (pure), `ChatMessage`'s status-transition shape, `ChatRepositoryImpl`'s
silent-refresh-and-retry branches (both the non-streaming shape reused verbatim from `EntriesRepositoryImpl`,
and the new first-frame-only streaming variant, research.md R3), and `ApiClient.sseStream()`'s own frame
parser (a `core/` addition — `test/core/network/`, mirroring where `error_mapper_test.dart`/similar already
live). `no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart` and `domain_purity_test.dart` both run unmodified against the new
`lib/features/chat/` folder with no exceptions needed.

**Target Platform**: iOS, portrait only — unchanged. No native project file touched.

**Project Type**: Same single Flutter mobile app. One new feature folder, `lib/features/chat/`
(domain/data/presentation, Principle V), plus two cross-cutting `core/network/` additions
(`ApiClient.sseStream()`/`SseFrame`, `ConnectivityChecker.onConnectivityChanged`) and in-place extensions to
`lib/features/home/` (`home_chat_shell_page.dart`'s composer, `app_drawer.dart`'s "CONVERSAS" section) and
`lib/core/routing/app_router.dart` (`/home`'s builder now wraps `MultiBlocProvider`). No backend/server code,
no change to `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`. No touch to `entries/`/`records/` — this unit never calls
`POST /entries` (FR-003/FR-014; that wiring belongs to RF10, explicitly out of scope).

**Performance Goals**: RNF01 unchanged. The optimistic local user+assistant placeholder pair (research.md R5)
is what keeps "a local action is reflected in the UI in under 100 ms" true for message-send despite the
network round-trip and SSE latency that necessarily follow it.

**Constraints**:
- No RF08 (proactive insight card)/RF10 (save-as-entry button)/persona-as-an-active-setting (extension) —
  `personaSnapshot` is read and stored exactly as the backend returns it at session creation, with no UI to
  change it (FR-014).
- No backend/contract/config change (FR-014) — `sseStream()`'s request shape and every parsed field name
  (research.md R2) are this app's own typed wrapper around what `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` and its
  own documented SSE sequence already describe; nothing new is sent the contract doesn't already define, and
  where the contract is silent on exact SSE field names, research.md documents the inferred shape explicitly
  as a judgment call rather than a verified fact.
- Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature (Principle V) — `chat/domain/` imports only `equatable`/`fpdart`;
  no `package:flutter`, no `chat/data/` class (confirmed against `domain_purity_test.dart`, unmodified).
  `ChatBloc`/`ChatSessionsBloc` depend only on `ChatRepository` (+ `ConnectivityChecker` for `ChatBloc` alone)
  — neither imports the other, nor `SessionBloc` (research.md R7; `no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart` unmodified,
  reinforced manually since both blocs sit in the same feature and so aren't mechanically checked against each
  other by that cross-feature-only test).
- "A single conversation never has two responses in flight at once" (FR-007) — the composer disables itself
  while `ChatReady.awaitingResponse` is true; no concurrent-request/generation-counter machinery is needed
  because no second write can even be dispatched while it's disabled (research.md R9).
- Zero visual values hardcoded outside `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (Principle IV/RNF08) — every new widget
  (chat bubbles, offline banner, composer) reuses existing tokens only (data-model.md's mapping table); zero
  new color/spacing/radius tokens needed, since the prototype's own chat-screen palette (`colorChatBubbleUser`,
  `colorInfoOffline`, `colorError`, etc.) was already added to `design_tokens.dart` during F000.

**Scale/Scope**: 1 new feature folder (`chat/`) with 5 domain entities/helpers, 1 repository interface, 2 data
classes + 1 repository impl, 2 blocs (+events/states), 5 new presentation widgets; 2 extended `core/network/`
classes (`ApiClient`, `ConnectivityChecker`); 2 existing `home/` files extended in place
(`home_chat_shell_page.dart`, `app_drawer.dart`); 1 route builder changed (`app_router.dart`'s `/home`); 5 new
DI registrations.

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-checked after Phase 1 design — see bottom of this section.*

| Principle / Standard | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| I. Product Source of Truth | PASS | `docs/input/` read-only. Every spot this plan resolves by reasonable technical judgment rather than reopening one of spec.md's own three already-resolved Clarifications — the SSE transport mechanism and inferred payload shapes (research.md R1/R2), mid-stream auth-expiry handling (R3), the local-cache shape (R4), optimistic local ids (R5), the title-preview length (R6), the two-bloc split and routing (R7), live-vs-synchronous offline handling (R8), single-flight gating (R9), retry's position-matching (R10), the GET-sourced `streaming`-status edge case (R11), the client-side length cap (R12), and why no extra use-case layer is introduced (R13) — is each built directly on spec.md's own FRs/Assumptions/Key Entities wording, never reopening a resolved Clarification. |
| II. Fixed Technology Stack | PASS | No new package. `flutter_bloc`/`fpdart`/`get_it`/Clean Architecture unchanged; SSE and live connectivity are both built on packages already in `pubspec.yaml` (`dio`, `connectivity_plus`). |
| III. Backend Boundary | PASS | Only already-contracted functions called (`chat-sessions-create`, `chat-sessions-list`, `chat-messages-list`, `chat-messages-send`, `chat-messages-retry` — `docs/input/backend/README.md`'s own path→function table); no AI provider called directly by the app (the backend's own Claude Sonnet 5/Voyage AI calls stay entirely server-side, consumed here only as the SSE response). |
| IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity | PASS | Every new widget reuses existing `DesignTokens` entries only (data-model.md's mapping table, sourced from prototype-extract.md §§2.2/3/6's own described chat-bubble/offline-banner/send-error-banner components) — zero new tokens. |
| V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention | PASS | `chat/domain/` imports only `equatable`/`fpdart` — confirmed against `domain_purity_test.dart` (unmodified, no exception needed). `ChatBloc`/`ChatSessionsBloc` each depend on exactly the repository (+ `ConnectivityChecker` for the former) they need, no cross-bloc import. |
| RNF01 (latency) | PASS | The optimistic local placeholder pair (research.md R5) is this unit's own mechanism for keeping message-send's *local* reflection under 100 ms despite the necessarily-slower network/SSE round-trip that follows it; any fetch exceeding 300 ms (session/history loads) shows the existing loading-indicator convention. |
| RNF02/03/04 (PII, retention, RLS) | N/A to RF04 | Backend-side; this unit's one write surface (`chat-messages-send`/`retry`) sends only the user's own typed text, same as every other authenticated write already does — no PII-detection logic is added here (RNF02 is explicitly backend-only, and chat messages are never run through the entries/PII pipeline at all per FR-003). |
| RNF05 (hard delete) | N/A to RF04 | Belongs to Settings/RNF05's own unit. |
| RNF06 (layer violations) | PASS | No `chat/domain/` file imports Flutter or a `chat/data/` class; neither bloc imports the other's file, nor `SessionBloc`'s — `no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart`/`domain_purity_test.dart` both continue to pass unmodified. |
| RNF07 (domain coverage ≥80%) | PASS (gate carried into tasks) | `chat_title_deriver.dart` is a pure, total function, as directly testable as `date_range_filter.dart` (RF06); `ChatMessage`'s status-transition shape and `ChatStreamEvent`'s sealed variants are plain data, trivially covered; `ChatRepositoryImpl`'s retry branches are testable against the same `mocktail` fakes `EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s own tests already use the pattern for. |
| RNF08 (visual fidelity) | PASS | Chat bubbles (user/assistant/streaming/failed), the offline banner, and the side menu's "CONVERSAS" section match prototype-extract.md §§2.2/6 exactly — no approximated layout or invented component beyond what the prototype already names. |
| RNF09 (Either + 15/15 error scenarios) | PASS (gate carried into tasks) | RF04 adds exactly one write endpoint whose *outcome shape* differs from every prior unit's (`chat-messages-send`'s streaming `Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>` per-frame, rather than a single `Either<Failure, T>`) — but it is still fully `Either`-typed throughout (Principle II), and its 3 required failure scenarios (timeout, malformed response, no-connection) are each exercised at the transport layer (`contracts/sse-transport-extension.md`'s own scenario table, implemented by tasks.md's T003) exactly as rigorously as any single-shot write endpoint's. `chat-sessions-create` is this unit's other write endpoint, tested the ordinary single-`Either` way. RNF09's project-wide "5 write endpoints × 3 failures = 15" tally gains these 2 (10/15 cumulative with RF01/RF02's existing 2 already counted — the full 5-endpoint tally completes across RF05/RF08/RF09/RF10's own later units). |

*Post-Phase-1 re-check: see "Post-Design Constitution Check" at the end of this document.*

## Project Structure

### Documentation (this feature)

```text
specs/007-chat-memory-rag/
├── plan.md                                  # This file
├── research.md                              # Phase 0 output
├── data-model.md                            # Phase 1 output
├── quickstart.md                            # Phase 1 output
├── contracts/                               # Phase 1 output
│   ├── sse-transport-extension.md
│   ├── chat-repository.md
│   ├── chat-bloc.md
│   └── chat-sessions-bloc.md
└── tasks.md                                 # Phase 2 output (/speckit-tasks — not created here)
```

### Source Code (repository root)

```text
cerne-ciclo-a/
└── lib/
    ├── core/
    │   ├── network/
    │   │   ├── api_client.dart                          # + sseStream() (research.md R1)
    │   │   ├── sse_frame.dart                            # NEW — SseFrame
    │   │   └── connectivity_checker.dart                 # + onConnectivityChanged (research.md R8)
    │   ├── di/
    │   │   └── service_locator.dart                      # + Chat registrations
    │   └── routing/
    │       └── app_router.dart                           # /home's builder wraps MultiBlocProvider
    └── features/
        ├── chat/
        │   ├── domain/
        │   │   ├── entities/
        │   │   │   ├── chat_session.dart                 # NEW — ChatPersona, ChatSession
        │   │   │   ├── chat_message.dart                 # NEW — ChatRole, ChatMessageStatus, ChatMessage
        │   │   │   ├── chat_sessions_page.dart            # NEW — mirrors EntriesPage
        │   │   │   ├── chat_stream_event.dart             # NEW — sealed ChatStreamEvent
        │   │   │   └── chat_title_deriver.dart            # NEW — pure title-preview function (research.md R6)
        │   │   └── repositories/
        │   │       └── chat_repository.dart               # NEW
        │   ├── data/
        │   │   ├── chat_remote_data_source.dart           # NEW — calls + SSE frame→event mapping
        │   │   ├── chat_local_cache.dart                  # NEW — Keychain-backed (research.md R4)
        │   │   └── chat_repository_impl.dart              # NEW
        │   └── presentation/
        │       ├── bloc/
        │       │   ├── chat_event.dart / chat_state.dart / chat_bloc.dart                  # NEW
        │       │   └── chat_sessions_event.dart / chat_sessions_state.dart / chat_sessions_bloc.dart  # NEW
        │       └── widgets/
        │           ├── chat_message_bubble.dart           # NEW
        │           ├── chat_composer.dart                 # NEW — replaces _ComposerBar
        │           └── chat_offline_banner.dart           # NEW
        └── home/
            └── presentation/
                ├── pages/
                │   └── home_chat_shell_page.dart          # extended — live ChatBloc wiring
                └── widgets/
                    └── app_drawer.dart                     # extended — "CONVERSAS" section + "Novo Chat"
```

**Structure Decision**: One new feature folder, `chat/`, following the exact three-layer convention every
prior unit already established — no deviation. The two `core/network/` additions
(`ApiClient.sseStream()`/`SseFrame`, `ConnectivityChecker.onConnectivityChanged`) live there rather than inside
`chat/` because neither is chat-specific in shape (any future SSE-consuming or connectivity-reactive unit
reuses them as-is, same reasoning RF01 already used placing `ConnectivityChecker` itself in `core/` rather than
inside `capture/`). `home/` is extended rather than folded into `chat/` because `home_chat_shell_page.dart`/
`app_drawer.dart` already exist as F000's own scaffold in that folder — moving them would be a gratuitous
rename with no behavioral benefit.

## Complexity Tracking

| Addition | Why Needed | Simpler Alternative Rejected Because |
|---|---|---|
| Hand-rolled SSE parsing in `ApiClient` (research.md R1) | `chat.messages.send`/`.retry` are this app's first and only streaming endpoints; the OpenAPI contract gives them no typed response shape (`text/event-stream`/`{type: string}`) for `call()`'s existing JSON-only path to handle | A third-party SSE package — rejected: introduces a second HTTP-stack assumption alongside `dio`, for a 5-event-type protocol spoken to exactly one backend (research.md R1) |
| Two blocs (`ChatBloc` + `ChatSessionsBloc`) instead of one | The live conversation (streaming, retry, composer gating) and the side menu's paginated list are independently-failing, independently-paginated concerns — exactly the two-concerns split `RecordsBloc` staying independent of `SessionBloc`/`VaultBloc` already establishes as this codebase's norm | One combined bloc — rejected: conflates two state shapes with genuinely different failure/pagination semantics into one, as reasoned in research.md R7 |
| A new `ChatLocalCache` (3 keys) rather than reusing `EntriesLocalCache`'s shape as-is | Chat needs to cache *two* independent things (a session list and N sessions' individual message histories) plus a small scalar (`lastActiveSessionId`) — `EntriesLocalCache` only ever caches one flat list | Reusing `EntriesLocalCache` directly — rejected: it has no concept of "per-session" keying, and bolting one on would make it do two unrelated jobs for two unrelated features |

*No entry needed beyond these three — each is either this unit's first genuinely new mechanism (SSE) or a
direct, justified extension of an already-proven pattern (two blocs mirroring `RecordsBloc`'s own split; a
cache mirroring `EntriesLocalCache`'s own rationale).*

## Post-Design Constitution Check

Re-evaluated after Phase 1 (data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md):

- `chat/domain/entities/*.dart` and `chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart` were re-checked against
  their actual planned imports: `equatable`, `fpdart` (for `ChatRepository`'s `Either`/`Stream` signatures),
  and `core/network/failure.dart` only. No `package:flutter`, no `chat/data/` class — RNF06/Principle V
  confirmed before any code exists.
- `ChatBloc`'s dependency surface was re-checked: exactly `ChatRepository` + `ConnectivityChecker` — no
  `SessionBloc`, no `ChatSessionsBloc` import. `ChatSessionsBloc`'s surface: exactly `ChatRepository` alone.
  Neither file appears in the other's import list (manually confirmed, since `no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart`
  only mechanically checks *across* `features/` folders, not within one).
- Re-checked `ApiClient.sseStream()`'s exception handling against `call()`'s existing `_mapException` — reused
  verbatim, no second, divergent failure-mapping implementation introduced.
- Re-checked that `ChatTitleDeriver`, the one domain helper RNF07 specifically needs to be independently
  testable, has zero constructor dependencies and zero I/O — confirmed pure in data-model.md's own listing.
- Re-checked the routing change (`app_router.dart`'s `/home` builder) against Principle V/research.md R7: no
  new `go_router` route, no `sessionId` path parameter — `AppRoutes.home` itself is unchanged.
- No change surfaces that touches `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, `.env`, any native iOS project file,
  or calls an AI provider directly — Principle III remains intact. No chat code path reaches `POST /entries`
  or any `entries/`-layer class — FR-003/FR-014 hold by construction (confirmed by `chat/`'s own import list
  containing nothing from `features/entries/`).

No new violations. Gate remains PASS.

4	import 'package:flutter_secure_storage/flutter_secure_storage.dart';
5	
6	/// On-device, cross-restart persistence for the entries the user has
7	/// already seen (the PRD's "local read cache" — requirements.md line 50/125:
8	/// results from it stay visible offline and reconcile with the server on
9	/// reconnect, with no duplicates). Keychain-backed, same pattern as
10	/// `VaultSecureStorage` — journal content is personal data, so it stays
11	/// encrypted at rest like the PIN it already sits behind.
12	///
13	/// Distinct from `EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s in-memory `cachedEntries`: that
14	/// field only ever held optimistic just-created entries for this process's
15	/// lifetime (research.md R8, 003-multimodal-capture). This class is what
16	/// makes that same list survive an app restart, which is what a cold open
17	/// on an already-offline device needs (closing snapshot at unit completion
18	/// did not cover this path — see Meus Registros intervention report).
19	class EntriesLocalCache {
20	  EntriesLocalCache({FlutterSecureStorage? storage})
21	    : _storage = storage ?? const FlutterSecureStorage();
22	
23	  final FlutterSecureStorage _storage;
24	
25	  static const _key = 'entriesLocalCache';
26	
27	  Future<List<Entry>> readAll() async {
28	    final raw = await _storage.read(key: _key);
29	    if (raw == null) return const [];
30	    try {
31	      final decoded = jsonDecode(raw) as List<dynamic>;
32	      return decoded.map((e) => _fromJson(e as Map<String, dynamic>)).toList();
33	    } on FormatException {
34	      return const [];
35	    } on TypeError {
36	      return const [];
37	    }
38	  }
39	
40	  Future<void> writeAll(List<Entry> entries) {
41	    final encoded = jsonEncode(entries.map(_toJson).toList());
42	    return _storage.write(key: _key, value: encoded);
43	  }
44	
45	  Map<String, dynamic> _toJson(Entry e) => {
46	    'id': e.id,
47	    'content': e.content,
48	    'source': e.source.name,
49	    'chatMessageId': e.chatMessageId,
50	    'occurredAt': e.occurredAt.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
51	    'tags': [
52	      for (final tag in e.tags) {'id': tag.id, 'name': tag.name},
53	    ],
54	    'piiStatus': e.piiStatus.name,
55	    'piiSpans': [
56	      for (final span in e.piiSpans)
57	        {'start': span.start, 'end': span.end, 'type': span.type},
58	    ],
59	    'embeddingStatus': e.embeddingStatus.name,
60	    'mediaDurationSeconds': e.mediaDurationSeconds,
61	    'serverRevision': e.serverRevision,
62	    'createdAt': e.createdAt.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
63	    'updatedAt': e.updatedAt.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
64	    'similarity': e.similarity,
65	  };
66	
67	  Entry _fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> data) => Entry(
68	    id: data['id'] as String,
69	    content: data['content'] as String,
70	    source: EntrySource.values.byName(data['source'] as String),
71	    chatMessageId: data['chatMessageId'] as String?,
72	    occurredAt: DateTime.parse(data['occurredAt'] as String),
73	    tags: (data['tags'] as List<dynamic>)
74	        .map(
75	          (t) => EntryTag(
76	            id: (t as Map<String, dynamic>)['id'] as String,
77	            name: t['name'] as String,
78	          ),
79	        )
80	        .toList(),
81	    piiStatus: PiiStatus.values.byName(data['piiStatus'] as String),
82	    piiSpans: (data['piiSpans'] as List<dynamic>)
83	        .map(
84	          (s) => PiiSpan(
85	            start: (s as Map<String, dynamic>)['start'] as int,
86	            end: s['end'] as int,
87	            type: s['type'] as String,
88	          ),
89	        )
90	        .toList(),
91	    embeddingStatus: EmbeddingStatus.values.byName(
92	      data['embeddingStatus'] as String,
93	    ),
94	    mediaDurationSeconds: data['mediaDurationSeconds'] as int?,
95	    serverRevision: data['serverRevision'] as int,
96	    createdAt: DateTime.parse(data['createdAt'] as String),
97	    updatedAt: DateTime.parse(data['updatedAt'] as String),
98	    similarity: (data['similarity'] as num?)?.toDouble(),
99	  );
100	}
